chunks: Ḥanān ibn Sadīr narrated from his father, who said:

I entered a bathhouse in al-Madīnah with my father, my grandfather, and my uncle. There was a man in the undressing room, and he said to us, “From which people are you?” We said, “From the people of al-ʿIrāq.” He said, “Which part of al-ʿIrāq?” We said, “The Kufans.” He said, “Welcome to you, O people of al-Kūfah, and greetings. You are the inner garment, not the outer covering.”

Then he said, “What prevents you from wearing a waistcloth? For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘The ʿawrah of a believer before another believer is inviolable.’” He said: So my uncle sent for a piece of cloth and split it into four parts. Then each one of us took one, and then we entered wearing them.

When we were in the hot room, he turned to my grandfather and said, “O old man, what prevents you from dyeing?” My grandfather said to him, “I met one who was better than me and you, and he did not dye.” He said, “And who is that, the one who is better than me?” He said, “I met ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام, and he did not dye.” So he lowered his head and perspired heavily, and said, “You have spoken the truth and done well.”

Then he said, “O old man, if you dye, then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did dye, and he is better than ʿAlī عليه السلام. And if you leave it, then in ʿAlī عليه السلام you have an example.”
He said: When we came out of the bathhouse, we asked about the man in the undressing room, and it was ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and with him was his son Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī عليهما السلام.

key_terms.الْإِزَارِ: a waistcloth used for covering the body
key_terms.الْمَسْلَخِ: the undressing or changing area of the bathhouse
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, whose bodily privacy is to be respected
key_terms.عَوْرَةُ: the private parts that must be concealed

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about bathhouse etiquette and dyeing the hair in the practice of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This narration recounts an encounter with Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام in a bathhouse, where he taught the etiquette of covering the ʿawrah and cited a hadith from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also records his balanced guidance regarding hair dye, affirming both the practice of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the example of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام.
